case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 227/88, decided on 20 November 1990

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the 4th respondent was unlawfully detained without being produced before a Magistrate within the time required by law, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed the 4th respondent was detained without being produced before a Magistrate within 24 hours as required, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued the 4th respondent was not under arrest until 4 November 1988 and was produced before the Magistrate on that date, complying with legal requirements.
key_facts: The 4th respondent was taken into police custody as a witness and later became a suspect.
He was formally arrested on 4 November 1988 and produced before the Magistrate the same day.
The petitioner argued detention from 2 November 1988 without production violated Article 13(2).
Respondents denied unlawful detention and asserted compliance with Sections 36 and 37 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 13(2) to require that a person arrested without a warrant must be produced before a Magistrate without unnecessary delay and within 24 hours exclusive of travel time. Detention without formal arrest does not trigger this requirement.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the 4th respondent was not under arrest until 4 November 1988 and was produced before the Magistrate on that date. The period before formal arrest was not detention under Article 13(2). Therefore, no violation occurred.
principles_established: Formal arrest is necessary to trigger the protections under Article 13(2).
Detention without formal arrest does not constitute unlawful detention under Article 13(2).
Production before a Magistrate within the prescribed time after arrest satisfies Article 13(2).
precedents_cited: Sections 36 and 37 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Act No. 15 of 1979
Explanation to Section 23 of the Code of Criminal Procedure
Piyasiri v. Fernando, A.S.P. (1988) 1 Sri L.R. 173

outcome.holding: The court held there was no violation of Article 13(2) as the 4th respondent was formally arrested on 4 November 1988 and produced before the Magistrate the same day, complying with the law.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) was central to the claim of unlawful detention without production before a judge. The court's interpretation and application of this clause led to dismissal of the claim under this article.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found the 4th respondent was formally arrested on 4 November 1988 and produced before the Magistrate on the same day, thus no unlawful detention violating Article 13(2) occurred.
